title: Jeremiah 10 — The idols of the nations and the living God

verdicts.reasoning: šimʿû ʾeṯ-haddāḇār ʾăšer dibber YHWH ʿălêḵem bêṯ yiśrāʾēl: 'to you' for ʿălêḵem and the vocative 'house of Israel' are exact.

Re-parsed kōh ʾāmar YHWH ... ʾal-tilmāḏû ... ʾal-tēḥāttû kî-yēḥattû haggôyim mēhēmmâ; the line is exact. The unquoted oracle follows the isaiah-woh practice (F4), and 'the signs of the skies' applies central ototh and shamayim in the physical register.
kî-ḥuqqôṯ hāʿammîm heḇel hûʾ kî-ʿēṣ miyyaʿar kərāṯô maʿăśēh yəḏê-ḥārāš bammaʿăṣāḏ: ASV structure, 'vanity' under hevel-vanity-latter-prophets. Exact.
yəyappēhû (sg.) 'he adorns it' and yəḥazzəqûm (pl. with 3mp suffix) 'they fasten it' follow the Hebrew number shift as the ASV does. wəlôʾ yāp̄îq 'so that it does not totter' is exact.

citations: HALOT s.v. miqšāh II; tōmer II
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed (ASV 'palm-tree, of turned work'). miqšâ is the cucumber field of Isa 1:8 and tōmer the post standing in it; 'a scarecrow in a cucumber field' is the standard modern reading, attested as early as Ep Jer 70. The rest of the verse (nāśôʾ yinnāśûʾ, inf. abs.) is exact. Not lens.

mēʾên kāmôḵā YHWH gāḏôl ʾattâ wəgāḏôl šimḵā biḡḇûrâ: exact. The MT plus (vv6-8, 10 absent from LXX and 4QJerb) is translated and the minus reported in commentary, which is correct corpus textual policy.
mî lōʾ yirāʾăḵā meleḵ haggôyim kî ləḵā yāʾāṯâ ...: 'it is your due' for yāʾâ and 'in all their kingdom' for malḵûṯām are exact.
ûḇəʾaḥaṯ yiḇʿărû wəyiḵsālû mûsar hăḇālîm ʿēṣ hûʾ: 'altogether' for bəʾaḥaṯ and the terse 'the instruction of vanities is wood' render the Hebrew without smoothing; the two readings are in commentary.
kesep̄ məruqqāʿ ... təḵēleṯ wəʾargāmān ... maʿăśēh ḥăḵāmîm kullām: exact; MT order kept and the LXX/4QJerb placement reported.

wayhwh ʾĕlōhîm ʾĕmeṯ hûʾ-ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm: 'the true God ... the living God' is the ASV/NRSV/NJPS rendering and the isaiah-woh convention; the plural adjective is reported in commentary. hāʾāreṣ parallel to gôyim gives 'earth' its universal scope (ASV, NRSV, NJPS). Line approved; the 'God'/'Elohim' corpus split is the open founder decision F1.

Re-read the Aramaic: kiḏnâ tēʾmərûn ləhôm ʾĕlāhayyāʾ dî-šəmayyāʾ wəʾarqāʾ lāʾ ʿăḇaḏû yēʾḇaḏû mēʾarʿāʾ ûmin-təḥôṯ šəmayyāʾ ʾēlleh. Disputed only for 'skies' against ASV 'heavens'; one English word for one sky across vv11-13 is a sound consistency rule, and the language switch, the ʿăḇaḏû / yēʾḇaḏû rhyme and the ʾarqāʾ/ʾarʿāʾ spellings are in commentary. Quotation marks are right for words the exiles are told to say.

ʿōśēh ʾereṣ bəḵōḥô mēḵîn tēḇēl bəḥoḵmāṯô ... nāṭâ šāmāyim: 'made the earth ... the world ... the skies' matches the creation set of Isa 40:22; 42:5 and the isaiah-woh rendering; 'earth' beside tēḇēl is the standard reading (ASV, NRSV, NJPS).

Ketiv ארץ / Qere hāʾāreṣ: the Qere is translated, a difference of the article only. ləqôl tittô hămôn mayim baššāmayim ... wayyôṣēʾ rûaḥ mēʾōṣərōṯāyw is rendered with the ASV; 'wind' for rûaḥ is physical. Exact.

nibʿar kol-ʾāḏām middaʿaṯ: the privative min 'without knowledge' is the ASV/NRSV/NJPS reading; KJV 'in his knowledge' is reported. Reception note verified against TBWTT ch. 3 (FR 'faute de science', EN 'brutish in his knowledge'), clearly labelled, and the English line carries no lens.
heḇel hēmmâ maʿăśēh taʿtuʿîm bəʿēṯ pəquddāṯām yōʾḇēḏû: exact.
lōʾ-ḵəʾēlleh ḥēleq yaʿăqōḇ kî-yôṣēr hakkōl hûʾ ...: 'former of all things' (yāṣar, central yatsar) and 'the tribe of his inheritance' are exact.

Ketiv ywšbty (archaic 2fs -tî) / Qere yōšeḇeṯ: same sense, the Qere is translated. Disputed: kinʿâ 'bundle' against ASV 'wares'. BDB glosses the hapax 'bundle, pack' and NRSV/NJPS have 'bundle'; it is the better-grounded rendering.
qôlēaʿ 'slinging out' and the objectless yimṣāʾû 'so that they may find it' keep the MT open, with the ASV supplement and the LXX passive in commentary. Exact.
ʾôy lî ʿal-šiḇrî naḥlâ makkāṯî ... ʾaḵ zeh ḥŏlî wəʾeśśāʾennû: ḥŏlî is pointed as the absolute noun, so 'a sickness' (not 'my') is accurate. Exact.
ʾohŏlî šuddāḏ wəḵol-mêṯāray nittāqû ...: exact rendering of the tent lament.
kî niḇʿărû hārōʿîm wəʾeṯ-YHWH lōʾ dārāšû ... hiśkîlû: exact; central darash-yhwh-seeking-oracle correctly applied.
qôl šəmûʿâ hinnēh ḇāʾâ wəraʿaš gāḏôl ... məʿôn tannîm: 'commotion' and 'jackals' (tannîm, not tannîn) are exact; the editor rightly declines to import the Ezekiel 'rumbling'.
yāḏaʿtî YHWH kî lōʾ lāʾāḏām darkô lōʾ-ləʾîš hōlēḵ wəhāḵîn ʾeṯ-ṣaʿăḏô: exact.
yassərēnî YHWH ʾaḵ-bəmišpāṭ ʾal-bəʾappəḵā pen-tamʿiṭēnî: 'in measure' is supported by the parallel ləmišpāṭ at Jer 30:11; 46:28. Exact.
šəp̄ōḵ ḥămāṯəḵā ... kî-ʾāḵəlû ʾeṯ-yaʿăqōḇ waʾăḵāluhû wayḵalluhû ...: exact; Ps 79:6-7 parallel noted.

glossaryReview.reasoning: direct is right for a presentation convention with no interpretive content. Verified in the lines: English names, 'the Lord YHWH' / 'the Lord', unquoted messenger formula (Jer 10:2, 18), quoted speech inside oracles and visions, and nəʾum 'declares' kept distinct from ʾāmar 'says' (Zech 4:6 against 5:4). Two open points are recorded under founder recommendations: F3, where the reviewer supports 'declares', and F4, where the reviewer supports ratification. Text identical in all five overlays (hash-checked).

Approve: the literal sense 'breath' and the idol polemic (Deut 32:21) are stated accurately, 'vanity' keeps the Jer 10:3/8/15 repetition, and the homograph central hevel (Abel) is correctly not extended.

Approve. 'scarecrow in a cucumber field' (miqšâ = Isa 1:8; Ep Jer 70) and 'bundle' (BDB) are better grounded than the ASV readings, and 10:18 and 10:24 keep the MT/ASV. direct is acceptable since both changed readings are lexicon- and commentary-backed.

Approve. The two-edition facts are accurate: vv6-8 and 10 are absent from the LXX, 4QJerb has the shorter order with v9 after 5a, and v11 is present in the LXX. Translating the MT consistently and reporting the shorter edition is defensible and honestly framed.

citations: EZK-WOH-43:2 (divergent practice, checked in the data)
glossaryReview.reasoning: Philologically the line is sound: in every LP1 site ʾĕlōhîm is either YHWH or the foreign gods set against him, and 'God'/'gods' is the ASV/NRSV/NJPS rendering and the isaiah-woh practice. Flagged only because this is the open founder decision F1 (published ezekiel-woh prints 'Elohim'), a project-stance call on the corpus's most visible term. Reviewer recommendation: ratify 'God' for the Latter Prophets.

direct is defensible because the scope test is applied from markers inside each verse: tēḇēl/šāmayim pairing, ʾăḏôn kol-hāʾāreṣ, ʾap̄sê-ʾāreṣ, 2 Chr 16:9. Every 'earth' site matches ASV or NRSV, and 'land' is kept for territory. Zeph 1:18 was tested and approved, with NRSV against ASV/NJPS, both in commentary.

Approve. The Aramaic facts are accurate (ʾarqāʾ/ʾarʿāʾ, the ʿăḇaḏû/yēʾḇaḏû rhyme, the Hebrew ʾēlleh), and one English word per referent across vv11-13 is a sound choice. Not marking the language switch typographically is consistent with corpus practice.

Sound: the lowercase 'spirit' at Zech 4:6 (YHWH's power against ḥayil/kōaḥ) and physical 'wind'/'breath' elsewhere follow the context, as in isaiah-woh. The Kings/Ezekiel 'ruach' divergence belongs to F1. Non-blocking: the claim that the ASV's capital reflects a 'later Trinitarian reading' is the editor's characterisation; check it against Meyers/Petersen before attributing it to them.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012)
BHS/WLC Ketiv-Qere at the three sites
glossaryReview.reasoning: Verified against the source: the three bracketed Ketiv/Qere pairs are Jer 10:13 (article), Jer 10:17 (archaic -tî) and Zech 4:2 (wyʾmr/wāʾōmar, sense-changing), and the Qere is translated at each. The versional readings listed are reported and not adopted, and the rafe at Zech 5:11 is handled correctly. direct is right for a textual policy consistent with the corpus.

Approve. The privative min is the ASV/RSV/NRSV/NJPS reading, and nēseḵ II 'cast image' is correctly separated from the libation homograph. The KJV wording of the canon's English is honestly reported, and the canon's French ('faute de science') does share the privative sense (verified, TBWTT ch. 3).

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked all 25 lines in the English alone. No English line reads as interpretation. The canon-cited verses (10:14) render the Hebrew at standard values, and each reception note is under its own 'Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim)' heading. Each note's quotation was verified against the canon text (TBWTT ch. 3 and ch. 5, FR/EN). Capitalisation (e.g. 'the Fish Gate') and vocabulary updates ('scroll', 'lampstand') are register or name conventions with lexical basis, not lens.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 109 LP1 lines, 31 overlay entries and 27 central ops were formed from the chapters, the sources, the drafts, the overlays and the diff, and recorded before wave-lp1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's watch points were each re-tested: Zeph 1:18 'earth', Zeph 1:10-11 names, Zech 4:14, Zech 9:9, Jer 10:5 and the unquoted Jer 10:2-5. The report does not mention the two Zech 4 speech-line issues (4:10 quote boundary; 4:13 'answered'), which stand as revise. The founder points F1-F5 are answered below.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-isaiah-aligned-conventions: Ratify for the Latter Prophets: 'God', 'earth'/'land' by scope, lowercase 'spirit', 'create' and 'oracle' are each the ASV/NRSV/NJPS-backed rendering and keep the five books one volume with Isaiah. Harmonize Ezekiel at its next wave, not by retro-editing signed-off chapters. The 'God'/'Elohim' split is the one item the reviewer flags for explicit founder ratification, because it is a project-stance choice.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-officials-shofar-vs-isaiah: Align Isaiah to 'officials' (Isa 32:1; 40:23; 43:28) and 'shofar' (Isa 27:13) at its next pass; both are lexically better grounded and already corpus rulings. Then promote megillah/menorah/sarim/shofar to central entries as the report proposes. Keep the Exodus 25 'lampstand' dependency on the Exodus checklist.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-neum-declares: Adopt 'declares YHWH' corpus-wide. Zechariah has ʾāmar YHWH (4:6) and nəʾum YHWH (5:4) within a few verses, and Isaiah's 'says' for both (e.g. ISA-14:22, checked) erases a distinction the Hebrew makes. Align Isaiah later.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-unquoted-messenger-formula: Ratify. At Jer 10:2-6 the Hebrew does not mark where the oracle ends, and leaving it unquoted avoids inventing a boundary. Related: at Zech 4:9-10 the wave's own marks run YHWH's word into the messenger's answer, which is the reviewer's revise at ZEC-WOH-4:10.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-sons-of-fresh-oil: Ship 'the two sons of fresh oil'. It is the most literal rendering, lexically grounded (yiṣhār, no māšaḥ), and inferred is the honest label; 'anointed ones' stays in commentary for reception continuity. If the founder wants a gentler line, 'the two sons of oil' (ASV margin) is the conservative literal fallback.

paragraphs.text: שִׁמְע֣וּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Hear the word that YHWH has spoken to you, house of Israel.

notes.official: *šimʿû ʾeṯ-haddāḇār* 'Hear the word' opens a unit (10:1-16) that sets the idols of the nations against YHWH the creator; vv12-16 recur almost word for word at 51:15-19. The chapter follows the shared Latter-Prophets conventions (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`): English name forms, 'God' for *ʾĕlōhîm*, 'earth' or 'land' by scope, and the oracle formula without quotation marks.

paragraphs.text: כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַגּוֹיִם֙ אַל־תִּלְמָ֔דוּ וּמֵאֹת֥וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם אַל־תֵּחָ֑תּוּ כִּֽי־יֵחַ֥תּוּ הַגּוֹיִ֖ם מֵהֵֽמָּה׃

i18n.en: Thus says YHWH: Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be dismayed at the signs of the skies, for the nations are dismayed at them.

notes.official: *kōh ʾāmar YHWH* 'Thus says YHWH' opens the oracle, and the divine speech that follows is not put in quotation marks (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`, the isaiah-woh practice). The Hebrew marks no end to the speech: vv2-5 address Israel about the idols of the nations, and v6 turns to address YHWH. The draft's closing mark after v5 was an editorial boundary the text does not draw, and it is removed. *ʾōṯôṯ haššāmayim* 'the signs of the skies' are celestial portents (eclipses, comets) read by the diviners of the nations (cf. Isa 47:13): *ʾôṯ* 'sign' as at Gen 1:14 (central `ototh`), *šāmayim* 'skies' in the physical register (central `shamayim`).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־חֻקּ֥וֹת הָֽעַמִּ֖ים הֶ֣בֶל ה֑וּא כִּֽי־עֵץ֙ מִיַּ֣עַר כְּרָת֔וֹ מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵ֥י־חָרָ֖שׁ בַּֽמַּעֲצָֽד׃

i18n.en: For the customs of the peoples are vanity: for it is a tree that one cuts out of the forest, the work of the hands of a craftsman with the axe.

notes.official: *ḥuqqôṯ hāʿammîm heḇel hûʾ* 'the customs of the peoples are vanity': *heḇel* is literally 'breath, vapor', and in the polemic against idols it names what has no substance (`hevel-vanity-latter-prophets`). The word returns at vv8 and 15. The singular *hûʾ* after the plural 'customs' already has the idol in view: what the customs produce is a block of wood cut from the forest. *maʿăṣāḏ* 'axe' (ASV), perhaps a carving tool (NJPS 'adz').

paragraphs.text: בְּכֶ֥סֶף וּבְזָהָ֖ב יְיַפֵּ֑הוּ בְּמַסְמְר֧וֹת וּבְמַקָּב֛וֹת יְחַזְּק֖וּם וְל֥וֹא יָפִֽיק׃

i18n.en: With silver and with gold he adorns it; with nails and with hammers they fasten it, so that it does not totter.

notes.official: *wəlôʾ yāp̄îq* 'so that it does not totter': an image that has to be nailed down in order to stand. Isa 40:20 and 41:7 use the same mockery.

paragraphs.text: כְּתֹ֨מֶר מִקְשָׁ֥ה הֵ֙מָּה֙ וְלֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ נָשׂ֥וֹא יִנָּשׂ֖וּא כִּ֣י לֹ֣א יִצְעָ֑דוּ אַל־תִּֽירְא֤וּ מֵהֶם֙ כִּי־לֹ֣א יָרֵ֔עוּ וְגַם־הֵיטֵ֖יב אֵ֥ין אוֹתָֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: They are like a scarecrow in a cucumber field, and they do not speak; they must surely be carried, for they do not walk. Do not be afraid of them, for they cannot do evil, nor is it in them to do good.

notes.official: *kəṯōmer miqšâ hēmmâ* 'They are like a scarecrow in a cucumber field'. *miqšâ* is the cucumber field of Isa 1:8, and the *tōmer* standing in it is a post or scarecrow, which neither speaks nor walks. The Letter of Jeremiah, the earliest commentary on this chapter, has the same image ('like a scarecrow in a cucumber bed', Ep Jer 70 = Bar 6:70), and NRSV, NJPS, Holladay (*Jeremiah 1*, Hermeneia, 1986) and Lundbom (AB 21A, 1999) read it so. The draft's ASV 'like a palm-tree, of turned work' combined *tōmer* 'palm' with *miqšâ* I 'hammered work' (overlay `lexical-cruxes-jeremiah-10`). *nāśôʾ yinnāśôʾ* 'they must surely be carried' (infinitive absolute), the contrast of Isa 46:1-7. The Old Greek and 4QJerᵇ break the verse after v5a and insert v9 there (overlay `mt-longer-edition-jeremiah-10`).

paragraphs.text: מֵאֵ֥ין כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה וְגָד֥וֹל שִׁמְךָ֖ בִּגְבוּרָֽה׃

i18n.en: There is none like you, YHWH; you are great, and your name is great in might.

notes.official: Verses 6-8 and 10 are absent from the Old Greek and from the Hebrew fragment 4QJerᵇ, which represent a shorter edition of the book (Tov, DJD 15, 1997). The line translates the Masoretic edition in full and in its order (overlay `mt-longer-edition-jeremiah-10`). The hymn turns from the idols to YHWH in the second person: *mēʾên kāmôḵā* 'There is none like you', where the prefixed *min* before *ʾên* is anomalous and usually taken as emphatic (Holladay).

paragraphs.text: מִ֣י לֹ֤א יִֽרָאֲךָ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם כִּ֥י לְךָ֖ יָאָ֑תָה כִּ֣י בְכָל־חַכְמֵ֧י הַגּוֹיִ֛ם וּבְכָל־מַלְכוּתָ֖ם מֵאֵ֥ין כָּמֽוֹךָ׃

i18n.en: Who would not fear you, King of the nations? For it is your due; for among all the wise of the nations and in all their kingdom there is none like you.

notes.official: MT only (see v6). *meleḵ haggôyim* 'King of the nations' is a vocative title found only here. *kî ləḵā yāʾāṯâ* 'for it is your due' (*yāʾâ* 'befit'). *ûḇəḵol-malḵûṯām* 'and in all their kingdom' (ASV 'in all their royal estate').

paragraphs.text: וּבְאַחַ֖ת יִבְעֲר֣וּ וְיִכְסָ֑לוּ מוּסַ֥ר הֲבָלִ֖ים עֵ֥ץ הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: But they are altogether brutish and foolish: the instruction of vanities is wood.

notes.official: MT only (see v6). *ûḇəʾaḥaṯ yiḇʿărû wəyiḵsālû* 'But they are altogether brutish and foolish': *bāʿar* 'be brutish' recurs at vv14 and 21. *mûsar hăḇālîm ʿēṣ hûʾ* 'the instruction of vanities is wood' is terse: the instruction the idols give is no more than wood, or the idol itself is a piece of wood. The plural *hăḇālîm* refers to the idols, as in Deut 32:21 (`hevel-vanity-latter-prophets`). ASV has 'the instruction of idols! it is but a stock'.

paragraphs.text: כֶּ֣סֶף מְרֻקָּ֞ע מִתַּרְשִׁ֣ישׁ יוּבָ֗א וְזָהָב֙ מֵֽאוּפָ֔ז מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חָרָ֖שׁ וִידֵ֣י צוֹרֵ֑ף תְּכֵ֤לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן֙ לְבוּשָׁ֔ם מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֲכָמִ֖ים כֻּלָּֽם׃

i18n.en: Silver beaten into plates is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the craftsman and of the hands of the goldsmith; blue and purple are their clothing; they are all the work of skilled men.

notes.official: *kesep̄ məruqqāʿ* 'Silver beaten into plates' from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz (unknown, perhaps a variant of Ophir; cf. Dan 10:5) clothe the image, and *təḵēleṯ wəʾargāmān* 'blue and purple' are the costly dyed fabrics of royal and cultic dress. In the Old Greek and 4QJerᵇ this verse stands inside v5; the line keeps the MT order (overlay `mt-longer-edition-jeremiah-10`).

paragraphs.text: וַֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ אֱמֶ֔ת הֽוּא־אֱלֹהִ֥ים חַיִּ֖ים וּמֶ֣לֶךְ עוֹלָ֑ם מִקִּצְפּוֹ֙ תִּרְעַ֣שׁ הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹֽא־יָכִ֥לוּ גוֹיִ֖ם זַעְמֽוֹ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: But YHWH is the true God; he is the living God and the everlasting King. At his wrath the earth quakes, and the nations cannot endure his indignation.

notes.official: *wayhwh ʾĕlōhîm ʾĕmeṯ* 'But YHWH is the true God'. *ʾĕlōhîm* is rendered 'God' under the shared convention (`elohim-god-latter-prophets`), as in isaiah-woh; the draft's 'Elohim' followed the Genesis-scoped central `elohim-as-translation`, which is not applied in these books. In *hûʾ-ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm* 'he is the living God' the adjective is plural, as in Deut 5:26 and 1 Sam 17:26, 36; it agrees with the plural form of the noun, and the singular *hûʾ* 'he' fixes the reference. *meleḵ ʿôlām* 'the everlasting King' (the central mlk-olam entry is scoped to the Ugaritic title and is not applied). *miqqiṣpô tirʿaš hāʾāreṣ* 'At his wrath the earth quakes': the parallel 'the nations' gives *hāʾāreṣ* its universal scope (`eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`; ASV, NRSV and NJPS 'the earth'), and the draft's 'the land' is replaced. The verse is absent from the Old Greek and 4QJerᵇ (overlay `mt-longer-edition-jeremiah-10`).

paragraphs.text: כִּדְנָה֙ תֵּאמְר֣וּן לְה֔וֹם אֱלָ֣הַיָּ֔א דִּֽי־שְׁמַיָּ֥א וְאַרְקָ֖א לָ֣א עֲבַ֑דוּ יֵאבַ֧דוּ מֵֽאַרְעָ֛א וּמִן־תְּח֥וֹת שְׁמַיָּ֖א אֵֽלֶּה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Thus you shall say to them: "The gods who did not make the skies and the earth — these shall perish from the earth and from under the skies."

notes.official: The verse is in Aramaic, the only Aramaic sentence in Jeremiah: a formula given to the exiles to say to the nations in the international language of the empire (overlay `aramaic-verse-jeremiah-10-11`; Holladay; Lundbom). It rhymes *ʿăḇaḏû* 'made' with *yēʾḇaḏû* 'shall perish', spells 'earth' two ways (*ʾarqāʾ*, *ʾarʿāʾ*), and ends with the Hebrew demonstrative *ʾēlleh* 'these'. The line renders the Aramaic by the rules that govern the Hebrew around it: lower-case 'gods' for *ʾĕlāhayyāʾ* (`elohim-god-latter-prophets`), and 'the skies and the earth' for the creation pair (`eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`; the 'skies' of central `shamayim`), as in vv12-13. The draft's ASV 'the heavens and the earth' is replaced so that one sky has one English word across vv11-13. Many commentators take the verse as an early addition to the idol polemic; it is present in the Old Greek.

paragraphs.text: עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֙רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ מֵכִ֥ין תֵּבֵ֖ל בְּחָכְמָת֑וֹ וּבִתְבוּנָת֖וֹ נָטָ֥ה שָׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: He who made the earth by his power, who established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the skies —

notes.official: Verses 12-16 recur as Jer 51:15-19. *ʿōśēh ʾereṣ bəḵōḥô* 'He who made the earth by his power' (central `asah`) resumes the subject of v10 across the Aramaic verse. *ʾereṣ*, *tēḇēl* 'world' and *šāmayim* are the creation set of Isa 40:22; 42:5; 44:24, rendered 'the earth ... the world ... the skies' (`eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`; central `shamayim`, as isaiah-woh's 'stretched out the skies'). The draft's 'the land' is replaced: in a creation doxology beside *tēḇēl* the word is the earth as a whole (ASV, NRSV, NJPS).

paragraphs.text: לְק֨וֹל תִּתּ֜וֹ הֲמ֥וֹן מַ֙יִם֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיַּעֲלֶ֥ה נְשִׂאִ֖ים מִקְצֵ֣ה ארץ [הָאָ֑רֶץ] בְּרָקִ֤ים לַמָּטָר֙ עָשָׂ֔ה וַיּ֥וֹצֵא ר֖וּחַ מֵאֹצְרֹתָֽיו׃

i18n.en: when he utters his voice, there is a tumult of waters in the skies, and he makes the vapors rise from the end of the earth; he makes lightnings for the rain, and brings out the wind from his treasuries.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: the consonantal text has *ʾereṣ* without the article, and the Qere *hāʾāreṣ* is translated, 'from the end of the earth' (`mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`; `eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`; Ps 135:7 repeats the clause). *ləqôl tittô hămôn mayim baššāmayim* 'when he utters his voice, there is a tumult of waters in the skies' (ASV; the voice is the thunder; central `mayim`, `shamayim`). *nəśiʾîm* 'vapors' (ASV; NRSV 'mist') are the rising clouds. *wayyôṣēʾ rûaḥ mēʾōṣərōṯāyw* 'and brings out the wind from his treasuries': physical wind (`ruach-spirit-wind-breath-latter-prophets`). NRSV has 'storehouses', the rendering of the central otzrot entry for the storehouses of snow and hail at Job 38:22, a different phrase that is not cited here.

paragraphs.text: נִבְעַ֤ר כָּל־אָדָם֙ מִדַּ֔עַת הֹבִ֥ישׁ כָּל־צוֹרֵ֖ף מִפָּ֑סֶל כִּ֛י שֶׁ֥קֶר נִסְכּ֖וֹ וְלֹא־ר֥וּחַ בָּֽם׃

i18n.en: Every man is brutish, without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his carved image; for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.

notes.official:
*nibʿar kol-ʾāḏām middaʿaṯ* 'Every man is brutish, without knowledge': the *min* is privative, 'without, for lack of' (ASV, NRSV, NJPS; overlay `nivar-middaat-brutish-without-knowledge-jeremiah-10-14`), while the KJV's 'brutish in his knowledge' takes it as the cause. *hōḇîš kol-ṣôrēp̄ mippāsel* 'every goldsmith is put to shame by his carved image' (central `pesel-utemunah-graven-image-iconographic-prohibition-cross-corpus`). *nisḵô* 'his molten image' is *nēseḵ* II 'cast image', not the drink-offering *nēseḵ* I. *wəlōʾ-rûaḥ bām* 'there is no breath in them' (`ruach-spirit-wind-breath-latter-prophets`; cf. Hab 2:19).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes the first clause, in French 'Tout homme est abruti, faute de science' and in its English printing 'Every man is brutish in his knowledge', and reads it of humanity's lack of the science that allowed the creators to create. The French has the privative sense that the line also has; the English printing follows the KJV wording. The line renders *daʿaṯ* 'knowledge' and does not specify what knowledge is lacking.

paragraphs.text: הֶ֣בֶל הֵ֔מָּה מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה תַּעְתֻּעִ֑ים בְּעֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֖ם יֹאבֵֽדוּ׃

i18n.en: They are vanity, a work of delusion; in the time of their visitation they shall perish.

notes.official: *heḇel hēmmâ maʿăśēh taʿtuʿîm* 'They are vanity, a work of delusion' (`hevel-vanity-latter-prophets`); *taʿtuʿîm* 'mockery, delusion'. *bəʿēṯ pəquddāṯām* 'in the time of their visitation', when YHWH calls them to account (*pqd*).

paragraphs.text: לֹֽא־כְאֵ֜לֶּה חֵ֣לֶק יַעֲקֹ֗ב כִּֽי־יוֹצֵ֤ר הַכֹּל֙ ה֔וּא וְיִ֨שְׂרָאֵ֔ל שֵׁ֖בֶט נַֽחֲלָת֑וֹ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Not like these is the portion of Jacob, for he is the former of all things, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance; YHWH of hosts is his name.

notes.official: *ḥēleq yaʿăqōḇ* 'the portion of Jacob' is YHWH himself, set against the idols (Deut 32:9; Ps 16:5). *yôṣēr hakkōl hûʾ* 'he is the former of all things': *yāṣar* 'form', the potter's verb (central `yatsar`). 'YHWH of hosts is his name' (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`; as Isa 48:2; 54:5).

paragraphs.text: אִסְפִּ֥י מֵאֶ֖רֶץ כִּנְעָתֵ֑ךְ ישבתי [יֹשֶׁ֖בֶת] בַּמָּצֽוֹר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Gather up your bundle from the land, you who dwell under siege.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: the consonantal *ywšbty* keeps the archaic second-feminine ending -tî; the Qere *yōšeḇeṯ* 'you (f.) who dwell' is translated, with no change of sense (`mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`). *ʾispî mēʾereṣ kinʿāṯēḵ* 'Gather up your bundle from the land': *kinʿâ* is a hapax for the pack a deportee carries (BDB 'bundle, pack'; NRSV, NJPS 'bundle'), and it replaces the ASV's 'wares' (overlay `lexical-cruxes-jeremiah-10`). Jerusalem under siege is addressed, and *ʾereṣ* is the land she must leave (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י קוֹלֵ֛עַ אֶת־יוֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ בַּפַּ֣עַם הַזֹּ֑את וַהֲצֵר֥וֹתִי לָהֶ֖ם לְמַ֥עַן יִמְצָֽאוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For thus says YHWH: Behold, I am slinging out the inhabitants of the land at this time, and I will bring distress on them, so that they may find it.

notes.official: *kî-ḵōh ʾāmar YHWH* 'For thus says YHWH' introduces the oracle without quotation marks (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`). *qôlēaʿ* 'slinging out', the image of the sling (1 Sam 25:29). *ləmaʿan yimṣāʾû* 'so that they may find it' has no object in the Hebrew: the ASV supplies 'feel it', and the Old Greek reads a passive, 'that the blow may be found'. The line keeps the open MT (overlay `lexical-cruxes-jeremiah-10`). *hāʾāreṣ* is the land of Judah (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: א֥וֹי לִי֙ עַל־שִׁבְרִ֔י נַחְלָ֖ה מַכָּתִ֑י וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי אַ֛ךְ זֶ֥ה חֳלִ֖י וְאֶשָּׂאֶֽנּוּ׃

i18n.en: Woe is me because of my hurt! My wound is grievous. But I said, "Truly this is a sickness, and I must bear it."

paragraphs.text: אָהֳלִ֣י שֻׁדָּ֔ד וְכָל־מֵיתָרַ֖י נִתָּ֑קוּ בָּנַ֤י יְצָאֻ֙נִי֙ וְאֵינָ֔ם אֵין־נֹטֶ֥ה עוֹד֙ אָהֳלִ֔י וּמֵקִ֖ים יְרִיעוֹתָֽי׃

i18n.en: My tent is laid waste, and all my cords are snapped; my children have gone out from me, and they are not; there is no one to stretch out my tent any more, and to set up my curtains.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י נִבְעֲרוּ֙ הָֽרֹעִ֔ים וְאֶת־יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֣א דָרָ֑שׁוּ עַל־כֵּן֙ לֹ֣א הִשְׂכִּ֔ילוּ וְכָל־מַרְעִיתָ֖ם נָפֽוֹצָה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For the shepherds have become brutish, and they have not inquired of YHWH; therefore they have not prospered, and all their flock is scattered.

notes.official: *nibʿărû hārōʿîm* 'the shepherds have become brutish': the rulers, 'shepherds' in the royal idiom of Jer 23:1-4, share the stupidity of the idol-makers (vv8, 14). *ʾeṯ-YHWH lōʾ dārāšû* 'they have not inquired of YHWH' (central `darash-yhwh-seeking-oracle`). *hiśkîlû* 'prospered' (ASV), or 'acted wisely'.

paragraphs.text: ק֤וֹל שְׁמוּעָה֙ הִנֵּ֣ה בָאָ֔ה וְרַ֥עַשׁ גָּד֖וֹל מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֑וֹן לָשׂ֞וּם אֶת־עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה שְׁמָמָ֖ה מְע֥וֹן תַּנִּֽים׃ (ס)

i18n.en: The sound of a report — behold, it comes, and a great commotion out of the land of the north, to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a dwelling of jackals.

notes.official: *qôl šəmûʿâ* 'The sound of a report'. *raʿaš gāḏôl* 'a great commotion' (ASV, NRSV), the noise of an army coming from the land of the north (central `eretz`). ezekiel-woh renders *raʿaš gāḏôl* 'a great rumbling' at Ezek 3:12-13, where it is the sound of the throne-chariot; that overlay decision is not imported here. *məʿôn tannîm* 'a dwelling of jackals': *tannîm* is the plural of *tan* 'jackal' (as isaiah-woh 13:22), not *tannîn* (central taninim 'great dragons').

paragraphs.text: יָדַ֣עְתִּי יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י לֹ֥א לָאָדָ֖ם דַּרְכּ֑וֹ לֹֽא־לְאִ֣ישׁ הֹלֵ֔ךְ וְהָכִ֖ין אֶֽת־צַעֲדֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: I know, YHWH, that the way of man is not his own; it is not in a man who walks to direct his steps.

paragraphs.text: יַסְּרֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה אַךְ־בְּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט אַל־בְּאַפְּךָ֖ פֶּן־תַּמְעִטֵֽנִי׃

i18n.en: Correct me, YHWH, but in measure; not in your anger, lest you bring me to nothing.

notes.official: *yassərēnî YHWH ʾaḵ-bəmišpāṭ* 'Correct me, YHWH, but in measure': *bəmišpāṭ* is the measured correction set against correction 'in your anger' (cf. Jer 30:11; 46:28 'in measure'). KJV has 'with judgment', NRSV 'in just measure' (overlay `lexical-cruxes-jeremiah-10`).

paragraphs.text: שְׁפֹ֣ךְ חֲמָתְךָ֗ עַל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יְדָע֔וּךָ וְעַל֙ מִשְׁפָּח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּשִׁמְךָ֖ לֹ֣א קָרָ֑אוּ כִּֽי־אָכְל֣וּ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַאֲכָלֻ֙הוּ֙ וַיְכַלֻּ֔הוּ וְאֶת־נָוֵ֖הוּ הֵשַֽׁמּוּ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, and on the families that do not call on your name; for they have devoured Jacob — they have devoured him and consumed him, and have laid waste his habitation.

notes.official: The verse is nearly identical to Ps 79:6-7.
